newsitem.title: JAPAN: Communist candidate assaulted in Japan campaign.
newsitem.headline: Communist candidate assaulted in Japan campaign.

text.p: In the first violence linked to Japan's forthcoming general elections, a candidate for the Communist Party was slightly injured on Tuesday when she was attacked by a man, a police spokesman said.
Sumi Fujita, 63, was struck by an unidentified man with what appeared to be a cane while making a speech in Osaka, western Japan, the spokesman said.
She suffered a slight injury to her waist and was taken to a local hospital, he said.
It was not clear why the man attacked Fujita, he said. No other details were immediately available.
Some analysts say the Japan Communist Party, which is fielding 321 candidates in Sunday's general elections, could sharply increase its Lower House seats to around 50 from 15.
The party, implacably hostile to the United States and other capitalist nations, has consistently attacked the government over its defence, nuclear power and economic policies.
In its election platform, the party promises to force U.S. troops out of Japan, scrap the Japan-U.S. Security Treaty and nullify a planned sales tax rise.
